questions.prompt: The bulk potential of the p-type body is negative. Write the threshold voltage, using the name VFB for the flat-band voltage, the name phip for that bulk potential, the name Cox for the oxide capacitance per area, the name q for the elementary charge, the name es for the silicon permittivity, and the name NA for the acceptor concentration.
questions.explanation: Threshold is three pieces: the flat-band voltage, the band bending \(-2\varphi_p\) (positive, because \(\varphi_p\) is negative), and the oxide drop that supports the depletion charge. That oxide drop is the depletion-charge magnitude divided by the oxide capacitance.

questions.prompt: Write the oxide-voltage term of the threshold, using the name QB for the magnitude of the depletion charge per area and the name Cox for the oxide capacitance per area.
questions.explanation: Supporting the depletion charge takes a voltage equal to that charge divided by the oxide capacitance. Halving the oxide thickness doubles the capacitance, so this term halves. The flat-band voltage and the band bending do not depend on the thickness.

questions.prompt: Doubling \(N_A\) changes all three \(V_T\) terms. Which changes the most (for \(N_A \sim 10^{17}\), \(t_{ox} = 5\ \mathrm{nm}\))?
options: The \(|Q_B|/C_{ox}\) term, which grows roughly as \(\sqrt{N_A}\); \(V_{FB}\) and \(-2\varphi_p\) change only by about \(V_{th}\ln2\)
questions.explanation:
Logarithmic terms: \(\Delta(-2\varphi_p) = 2V_{th}\ln2 \approx 36\ \mathrm{mV}\) and \(\Delta V_{FB} = -18\ \mathrm{mV}\). Square-root term: \(\times\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt{1+\ldots}\), about \(+0.11\ \mathrm{V}\) here.
Gotcha: doubling the doping does NOT double \(V_T\).

questions.prompt: A worked solution writes the band-bending term of the threshold for p-type silicon. Exactly one step is wrong.
questions.explanation: Adding twice a negative bulk potential subtracts a positive voltage. The bend from \(\varphi_p\) to \(-\varphi_p\) is \(-2\varphi_p\), which is positive and must be added.
steps: For p-type silicon the bulk potential is negative.
Threshold bends the surface from that bulk potential to the negative of the bulk potential.
The bend is minus twice the bulk potential, and that quantity is positive.
The threshold formula therefore adds twice the bulk potential itself.
reasons: The bend is minus twice the bulk potential, so adding twice the bulk potential itself has the wrong sign.
Twice the bulk potential is already positive, so adding it is the right band bending.

questions.prompt: A body bias \(V_{SB}\) adds to the needed silicon drop, changing \(|Q_B|\) to \(\sqrt{2q\varepsilon_sN_A(-2\varphi_p + V_{SB})}\). For the \(N_A = 10^{17}\), \(t_{ox} = 5\ \mathrm{nm}\) device with \(V_{SB} = 1\ \mathrm{V}\), by how much does \(V_T\) rise, in V?
questions.explanation:
\[\Delta V_T = \frac{\sqrt{2q\varepsilon_sN_A}}{C_{ox}}\left(\sqrt{-2\varphi_p + V_{SB}} - \sqrt{-2\varphi_p}\right) = \gamma(\sqrt{1.838} - \sqrt{0.838})\]
\[\gamma = 0.264\ \sqrt{\mathrm{V}} \Rightarrow \Delta V_T \approx 0.116\ \mathrm{V}\]
Gotcha: the change goes as a square root, not linearly with \(V_{SB}\).

questions.prompt: Preview of drive: the \(N_A = 10^{17}\), \(t_{ox} = 5\ \mathrm{nm}\) device (\(V_T \approx 0.111\ \mathrm{V}\)) is biased at \(V_{GB} = 1.5\ \mathrm{V}\). What is the inversion electron density \(C_{ox}(V_{GB}-V_T)/q\), in cm⁻²? Scientific notation is fine.
questions.explanation:
\[n_s = \frac{(6.9\times10^{-7})(1.5 - 0.111)}{1.602\times10^{-19}} \approx 5.99\times10^{12}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}\]
This sheet charge carries the MOSFET current.

questions.prompt: Preview of body bias: the reverse source-to-body bias \(V_{SB}\) raises \(V_T\) as above. Where does this matter in circuits?
options: In stacked transistors (e.g. the upper NMOS in a NAND gate or a source follower), whose sources sit above ground, so their V_T is higher
Nowhere; the body is always tied to the source
Only in the oxide breakdown rating
questions.explanation: Any NMOS whose source is not at the body (ground) potential sees \(V_{SB} > 0\). This 'body effect' reduces the drive and the gain of a source follower.

questions.prompt: Preview of PMOS: for a p+ poly gate on n-type silicon, what's the sign of \(V_T\), and what gate voltage turns the device on?
options: V_T is negative; the gate must go below V_T (more negative) to invert the n-surface into a hole channel
Negative, but a positive gate turns it on
questions.explanation: Everything mirrors: \(\varphi_n > 0\), so the band bending is \(-2\varphi_n < 0\), and the depletion charge is positive donors, so the oxide term is negative. Holes form the channel.
